newsitem.title: USA: Stocks mixed, await key economic data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks mixed, await key economic data.

text.p: Stock prices were mixed Tuesday as traders mostly kept to the sidelines, waiting for key economic data due Wednesday and Thursday.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 13.01 points at 8,049.10.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 16-10 on volume of 277 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index was up 9.09 points at 1,595.83.
"You have to be extremely aggressive to take a big position ahead of numbers coming out the rest of the week," said Charles Payne of Wall Street Strategies.

The bond market was erratic, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond up 14/32, or $4.375 on a $1,000 bond, after gaining 20/32 initially, and the yield slipping to 6.61 percent from 6.64 percent at Monday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
"The breadth of the market is pretty good," said Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney. "The techs are having a pretty good day."
"But I don't see the Dow doing that much. Everyone is waiting for the inflation data and then take it from there," he said.

July retail sales data, due Wednesday, were forecast to rise 0.7 percent after a 0.5 percent gain in June. The July producer price index is set for release Wednesday and the consumer price index Thursday.
Among individual stocks, Nordstrom Inc. rose 1/8 to 58 after posting better-than-expected earnings.
Quick & Reilly Group Inc. led selected brokerage stocks higher early, the gain sparked by reports of a possible sale of Quick to perhaps a large Southern bank.
Quick's stock hit a year high of 32-11/16 before easing to 32-3/8, up 3-1/16 on the day.
Amgen Inc. tumbled to a year low of 52 before easing back to 52-1/4, down 4-15/16, after it said earnings expectations for its key Epogen drug were reduced.
